title: Support and ideal-power torsion of finite dual Koszul stages
statement: Let $C$ be a small site with topology $T$, let $R$ be a commutative ring sheaf, let $r,n\in\mathbf N$, and let $b_1,\ldots,b_r$ be global sections of $R$. Write $D_n$ for the actual internal dual of the ordered positive Koszul complex on $b_j^{n+1}$, as in [def-weil-pbc-ringed-koszul-system]. Then $D_n^i=0$ for $i<-r$ or $i>0$. For every integer $q$, every object $U$ of the site, every $a\in(b_1(U),\ldots,b_r(U))^{r(n+1)+1}$ and every local section $x\in H^q(D_n)(U)$, one has $ax=0$. The empty list and the zero ring are allowed.

source.place: Tag 0913, lemma-extended-alternating-Cech-is-colimit-koszul, generator contractions; algebraization.tex Tag 0A0E, lemma-derived-completion-koszul, finite free duality.

proof.text: In the negative two-term factor, the identity from degree zero to degree minus one contracts multiplication by the differential scalar. Tensor this contraction across the ordered factors, using naturality of scalar multiplication and the signed tensor homotopy formulas. Thus each generator to power n+1 acts by zero on all homology sheaves. Apply the finite-generator pigeonhole inclusion from the ordered positive Koszul torsion argument to put the displayed ideal power in the annihilator.

The constructed negative-to-internal-dual isomorphism transports the scalar annihilation. The positive ordered tensor is zero outside [0,r], by induction with its two-row total decomposition. The internal dual in degree i is Hom from its positive degree -i term into R, giving support [-r,0].

theorem dualKoszul_bounded_torsion
    (R : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{u}) (r : ℕ)
    (b : Fin r → (R.obj ⋙ forget CommRingCat).sections) (n : ℕ) :
    (∀ i : ℤ, i < -(r : ℤ) ∨ 0 < i →
      IsZero (((ringedKoszulDualTower R r b).obj (op n)).X i)) ∧
    (∀ (q : ℤ) (X : Cᵒᵖ) (a : R.obj.obj X),
      a ∈ (Ideal.span (Set.range (fun j : Fin r ↦ (b j).val X))) ^
        (r * (n + 1) + 1) →
      ∀ x : ((((ringedKoszulDualTower R r b).obj (op n)).homology q).val.obj X),
        a • x = 0)
